topic: Penner pre-integrated curvature skin subsurface scattering vs hard Lambert terminator rig
topic_zh: Penner 预积分曲率驱动皮肤次表面散射（SSS）对比硬 Lambert 明暗交界线死黑
scope: Deterministic Eric Penner (2011) pre-integrated curvature-driven subsurface scattering (I_c(theta, kappa*l_c)) versus naive hard Lambertian clamping max(0, N.L) and 256-tap numerical arc quadrature across 17 terminator angles (theta in [10, 170] deg). No neural portrait relighting execution.

timing_note: Median of 7 alternating Node CPU runs after warmup. Closed-form antiderivative pre-integrated SSS evaluation versus 256-tap numerical arc quadrature.

protocol.function: I_c(θ, κℓ_c) = [sin(min(π/2, θ+κℓ_c)) − sin(max(−π/2, θ−κℓ_c))]/(2κℓ_c) → θ=90° I_R = 0.1724 (> 5.7× I_B)

robustness.name: Sampled 17 terminator angles preserve smooth RGB wavelength-dependent subsurface scattering without hard-Lambert cutoff

good_fit: Real-time digital human faces, ears, noses, fingers, wax candles, and translucent jade props on mobile/WebGL2/VR
Explaining why longer red mean free path (ℓ_R=1.2mm vs ℓ_B=0.2mm) produces a 5.75× crimson warmth band across the θ=90° shadow terminator
Parameterized 2D (N·L, κ) pre-integrated skin LUTs driven by screen-space curvature κ = ‖∇N‖ / ‖∇P‖
Replacing 256-tap numerical diffusion integrals or 6-pass texture-space blurs with O(1) closed-form pre-integration
not_for: Large flat skin regions with high-frequency shadow maps where Separable Screen-Space SSS (Jiménez SSSSS) is needed
Opaque metallic or stone surfaces with zero subsurface mean free path (ℓ = 0)
Neural portrait relighting or diffusion-based face synthesis models
Thin back-lit ear pinnae transilluminated from behind (requires thickness map transmittance exp(-σ_t d))
